sayfalar.1:
Earnings Release – 3Q26
                                                                                        05 November 2026



  Strategic Focus Areas Lead to a Strong Performance;
     3Q26 EBITDA Margin increased by 7pp to 20%
Doğan Holding’s Net Asset Value came in at 3.2 billion USD as of 3Q26 (13% ytd),
and the Group recorded 30.0 billion TL in revenues, 6.0 billion TL in EBITDA, and
2.0 billion TL in net profit in the third quarter of 2026. During the quarter, EBITDA
margin increased by 7pp y/y and reached 20%.

NAV Changes*:




              *Please see NAV table in the annex for detailed valuation information


Key Highlights of 3Q26:

• Doğan Holding’s total revenues came in at 30.0 billion TL in 3Q26 (+6% y/y).
  Strong growth at Hepiyi, Gümüştaş and D Investment Bank more than offset the
  softer performance in the energy and automotive segments. Excluding the
  automotive segment, revenue growth was 11% y/y in 3Q26.

• Meanwhile, EBITDA came in at 6.0 billion TL in 3Q26, +64% y/y in real
  terms. Lower labour costs at Karel following its operational turnaround,
  stronger output at Gümüştaş and tight cost control at Galata Wind supported
  profitability, bringing the consolidated EBITDA margin to 20% (3Q25:
  13%).

• Net Asset Value (NAV) came in at 3,194 million USD as of end-September 2026
  (13% ytd). The change was primarily driven by the finance segment (+241
  million USD) and Gümüştaş Mining (+194 million USD). The share of Strategic
  Focus Areas within NAV stood at 57% (3Q25: 48%).

• The Holding’s standalone net cash position came in at 645 million USD (+5%
  y/y; 9M25: 617 million USD). No capital injections were required for any
  subsidiary during the third quarter. Compared to previous year, the share of TL-
  denominated assets within our standalone net cash changed from 14% to 18%.

• Our strategic focus areas continue to deliver strong results in 2026:
⎯ Mining: Gümüştaş recorded 63% revenue growth y/y and a 54% EBITDA
   margin in 9M26, compared with its FY26 guidance of at least 40% revenue
   growth and a 40–50% EBITDA margin. The company achieved a 46% y/y
   increase in ore production in 9M26 and completed the capacity expansion at
   its processing facility, which has been operating at target capacity since October.

⎯ Financial services: Hepiyi Sigorta’s Assets Under Management (AUM)
 increased by 41% y/y to 985 million USD. Supported by its disciplined and
 profitable growth strategy, the company continued to gain market share in
 written premiums, with its share rising by 109 bps y/y to 7.1% in MTPL
 insurance and by 45 bps y/y to 4.6% in the MOD segment. Leveraging Artificial
 Intelligence in its claims payment operations, the company has become the
 fastest claims-paying insurer in MOD segment as per June industry data. In
 3Q26, gross written premiums grew by 45% y/y to 10.4 billion TL, while net
 profit more than doubled (+113% y/y) to 2.6 billion TL (excluding TAS 29).

⎯ Renewable energy: Galata Wind maintained its installed capacity at 354 MW
  during 3Q26. Galata Wind’s electricity generation declined by 5% y/y in 3Q26,
  while Türkiye’s total generation rose by 0.4% y/y on the back of a 96% increase
  in hydroelectric output. The USD-based Market Clearing Price (MCP) declined
  by 18% y/y to 58 USD, recovering from 20 USD in 2Q26. Revenue declined by
  29% y/y in real terms; however, the EBITDA margin recovered to 62% (2Q26:
  33%) on the back of controlled operating expenses and recovering MCP. Net
  profit came in at 313 million TL in 3Q26.

• Doğan Holding outperformed the Holding Index in 9M26, delivering a total
  return of 8.4% year-to-date versus -17.2% for the index, implying a 26 pp
  outperformance. The share of foreign investors in the free float also
  increased by 8.8 pp y/y, from 18.5% to 27.3% as of end-September 2026, while
  the share of institutional investors reached 57.4%.

Comments of Çağlar Göğüş, Dogan Holding CEO:

Our strategic focus areas once again set the performance for the Group in the third
quarter. Gümüştaş Mining increased its ore production by 46% y/y in 9M26 and
completed the capacity expansion at its processing facility, which has been
operating at the target capacity since October. Hepiyi Sigorta grew its assets under
management to 985 million USD and more than doubled its net profit y/y.

Our Net Asset Value stood at 3.2 billion USD (13% YTD) and our consolidated
EBITDA came in at 14.4 billion TL in 9M26, with an EBITDA margin of 17.0%
with a balanced contribution from all verticals. This success is the result of our
holding portfolio reshaping. Looking at our acquisitions and exits over the past
five years, we see that we have exited investments generating low single-digit
IRRs, while companies delivering double-digit IRRs and creating strategic
value to our country have been added to the holding portfolio. In other words,
we have been selectively reallocating our portfolio toward businesses with higher
return potential, at the same time, by streamlining our portfolio, we are able to
focus more on our existing businesses and drive performance improvements. In
line with this strategic direction, we have signed an agreement for the sale of

Kanal D Romania in late October, at an enterprise value of 109 million EUR, as
part of our ongoing efforts to streamline our portfolio. In addition, we restructured
Dogan Trend’s motorcycle operations in October to focus our financial and
organizational resources on our core automotive brands, Suzuki, MG and Maxus.

The rest of the portfolio further reinforced this picture. Increased ore production
and processing coupled with high-quality pyrite concentrate at Gümüştaş drove
further EBITDA growth; Galata Wind kept its EBITDA margin above 60% despite
y/y lower electricity prices, thanks to tight cost control, while Karel continued to
reflect the impact of its ongoing operational transformation and hence delivered
20% EBITDA margin in 3Q26 vs 10% a year ago. Investments continued alongside
ongoing EBITDA margin improvements across the portfolio. During the period,
Galata Wind pressed ahead with its power generation and energy storage
investments in Türkiye and abroad, while Karel strengthened its leading position
in communication technologies and, as part of its operational transformation,
continued to make strides in its higher-margin manufacturing and automotive
business lines.

Above all, this quarter confirms that our portfolio is evolving exactly as we
intended. With the share of our strategic focus companies in total Net Asset
Value at 57% (48% a year ago), our revenue and EBITDA composition has
become healthier, more balanced and more resilient to cyclical shifts. We are
delivering growth exactly where we want it, reinforcing our confidence in
achieving our USD 4.5 billion Net Asset Value target by 2030.

Key Developments Across Business Lines

1-) Strategic Focus Areas:

Mining – Gümüştaş Mining
• Gümüştaş continued to deliver strong operational results in the third quarter,
  supported by higher production and high-quality pyrite concentrate sales from
  Gümüşhane.
• In this context, ore production rose by 35% y/y to 198 thousand tons in the
  third quarter (9M26: +46% y/y); total revenues increased by 82%, while the
  EBITDA margin came in at 57% in 3Q26 (3Q25: 39%).
• Gümüştaş completed 53 million USD of capital expenditure in 9M26,
  directed towards the commissioning of a Dense Media Separation (DMS)
  plant, a capacity increase at the flotation processing facility, and the expansion
  of the production area. With the completion of the capacity expansion, the plant
  has been operating at the target capacity since October, raising annual ore
  processing capacity to 840 thousand tons from 600 thousand tons.

Financial Services – Hepiyi Insurance

• Assets Under Management (AUM) reached 985 million USD as of
  September 2026, representing a 41% y/y increase, reflecting continued
  balance sheet strengthening, supported particularly by effective portfolio
  management.
• Gross Written Premiums (GWP) maintained their strong growth momentum,
  increasing 45% y/y in 3Q26 as competition eased from the second quarter
  onwards. Excluding the impact of IAS 29, net profit more than doubled, rising
  113% y/y to 2.6 billion TL, bringing the 9M26 return on equity to 74%.
• Hepiyi Sigorta further strengthened its market position in written premiums
  by continuing to gain market share. Its market share in the compulsory motor
  third-party liability (MTPL) segment increased by 109 basis points y/y to
  7.1%, while its motor own damage (MOD) market share rose by 45 basis
  points to 4.6%. This performance positioned Hepiyi Sigorta as Türkiye’s 3rd
  largest MTPL insurer and 7th largest MOD insurer.
• Supported by its digital operating platform, Hepiyi Sigorta maintained an
  OPEX/revenue ratio of 5.0%, significantly below the latest industry average
  of 10.1%, underscoring operational efficiency as a key competitive
  differentiator. This operational excellence also enabled Hepiyi Sigorta as the
  fastest claims-paying insurer in Türkiye in MOD segment as per June
  industry data.

2-) Dynamic Focus Areas:

Electronics, Technology & Industry – Karel

• The transformation program at Karel continued to deliver positive results. As a
  result, Karel recorded real growth of 4% y/y in the third quarter.
• On top of the increased share of high-margin segments, the strategic
  downsizing of the electronic card manufacturing business line, together with
  lower labour costs following the completion of headcount optimization paved
  the way for Karel to improve its consolidated EBITDA margin to 20% in
  3Q26, similar to the y/y improvements realized in the previous quarters,
  confirming the effectiveness of operational turnaround actions.
• The improvement in the financial outlook continued in 3Q26, supported by
  ongoing discipline in working capital management, with a focus on cash
  generation and inventory reduction. However, high financing costs continued
  to weigh on the bottom line, resulting in a net loss of 481 million TL in 3Q26.

Electronics, Technology & Industry– Sesa Packaging

• Domestic orders slightly declined in 3Q26 q/q, as customers pulled
  forward their demand to 2Q26 amid closures at Strait of Hormuz. In
  addition, EUR/TL lagging behind inflation and a narrowing spread between
  raw material costs and selling prices weighed on the EBITDA margin. In the
  third quarter, the company recorded net income of 88 million TL.
• The share of premium products in total revenue increased to 31% in 3Q26.
• The favorable geographic mix of exports was supported by new customers:
  While the overall export contribution declined to 49% (3Q25: 53%), the
  combined share of the United Kingdom and the USA in total exports reached
  42%, supported by new customer acquisitions.

Automotive & Mobility – Doğan Trend

• MG sales increased by 178% y/y in 3Q26, rising from 307 units to 854 units,
  thanks to competitive pricing and the contribution from newly launched
  models in 1Q26, despite a 23% y/y contraction in Türkiye’s automotive
  market. Suzuki sales declined by 43% y/y to 919 units. The weaker
  performance was primarily attributable to the discontinuation of Suzuki
  Swift model sales following higher customs duties on imports from Japan and
  limited access to consumer financing for cars.
• In October, Doğan Trend restructured its motorcycle operations, ending the
  production and sales operations of Kymco in Türkiye and the Piaggio Group
  motorcycle operations (Vespa, Aprilia, Moto Guzzi and Piaggio), while
  continuing its marine engine distributorship without interruption. This
  strategic step allows the company to focus its financial and organizational
  resources on its core automotive operations, led by Suzuki, MG and Maxus.
• Accordingly, total revenues came in at 3,612 mn TL in 3Q26 (-21% y/y), while
  EBITDA came in at -129 mn TL. Net loss came in at 470 mn TL (3Q25: 472 mn
  TL).

the business world when Honorary Chairperson Aydın Doğan registered with the Mecidiyeköy
Tax Office in 1959 and founded his first automotive company in 1961. Today, Doğan Group
companies play a pioneering role with their innovative vision in the fields of electricity
generation, industry & trade, mining, automotive trade & marketing, finance & investment,
internet & entertainment, and real estate.
Doğan Group's corporate and ethical values, which are implemented by all of its companies, set
an example for other organizations in the business world. Aiming for global success in its
production and commercial activities, Doğan Group closely monitors developments in Türkiye
and abroad and conducts its operations efficiently through strategic collaborations with
international groups.
